runner: sh evals/run.sh (it launches Chrome, so run it outside Claude Code's Bash sandbox)

evals.name: example-intro-15s-16x9
evals.prompt: Make a 15-second 16:9 intro video for Example Co. (a fictional furniture shop). Use the colors, fonts and logo from brand.json (main #2F5D50 / accent #6B4E9B / sub #3F9C94 / support #C5D86D).
evals.expected_output: Stops once at the storyboard (scene table + representative frames + contact/strip/phone); after approval, outputs a 1920x1080, 60fps, 900-frame mp4 with sound plus poster/contact/README/source. Two renders give the same mp4 hash. The final render stops before approval and after changes made post-approval.
assertions: storyboard outputs storyboard.md / storyboard.json, one representative frame per scene, and contact/strip/phone
determinism check (same frame drawn twice, hashes match) is OK
the brand.json primary color covers enough area in the representative frames
final before approval stops with exit 3 and makes no mp4
1920x1080, 60fps, 900 frames, H.264/yuv420p, aac
poster.png / contact.png / README.md / manifest.json / source/ are in the deliverables
mp4 loudness is -14 LUFS ±1 with true peak at or below -1 dBFS
sha256 of two mp4 renders match
changing video.js after approval makes both final and approve stop with exit 3

evals.name: media-mix-image-and-clip-30fps
evals.prompt: Make a 5-second intro cut at 30fps featuring a screenshot of the admin panel (assets/screenshot.png) and a screen recording (clips/demo.mp4).
evals.expected_output: A 1920x1080, 30fps, 150-frame mp4 where both the screenshot (image asset) and the live-action clip appear on screen. The clip is drawn from frames extracted into a sequence, not played back by the browser, and at least 2 distinct frames are used.
assertions: storyboard outputs representative frames and evidence, and the determinism check is OK
1920x1080, 30fps (a non-default value other than 60 takes effect), 150 frames
the image asset (screenshot) was actually drawn (render manifest)
at least 2 distinct live-action clip frames were drawn (render manifest)
in an SFX-only video, stretches without cues are silent (no BGM added on its own)
sha256 of two mp4 renders match

evals.name: multi-aspect-9x16-1x1-16x9-loop
evals.prompt: Export the same scenes in 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9. I want a 4-second loop for social media.
evals.expected_output: Three videos from the same video.js: 1080x1920 / 1080x1080 / 1920x1080. Storyboards come out for all three aspects, and the loop seam check (seam.png and the continuity verdict) is OK. Two renders of each aspect give matching sha256.
assertions: representative frames and evidence (including seam) for all 3 aspects
the loop seam continuity check is OK
sha256 of two mp4 renders match for all 3 aspects

evals.name: bgm-calm-8s
evals.prompt: Add BGM to a short 8-second cut. Chords Am → F → C → G, calm feel. Keep the sound effects as before.
evals.expected_output: A 1920x1080, 60fps, 480-frame mp4 mixing BGM composed from the chord progression and style (MIDI → FluidSynth) with sound effects. preview.wav and a spectrogram come out at the storyboard stage. mp4 loudness is -14 LUFS ±1 with true peak at or below -1 dBFS. Two renders give the same sha256.
assertions: storyboard outputs representative frames and evidence, and the determinism check is OK
preview.wav and spectrogram.png come out at the storyboard stage, and the BGM is composed in the specified style
1920x1080, 60fps, 480 frames, H.264/yuv420p, aac
mp4 loudness is -14 LUFS ±1 with true peak at or below -1 dBFS
BGM is audible in stretches without sound effects
the manifest records the BGM (style, soundfont, MIDI hash)
sha256 of two mp4 renders match

evals.name: cutsheet-feedback-v1-v2
evals.prompt: Show me the storyboard as a cut sheet. I'll write what to fix in the FB column; give me the next version with those fixes. Keep the previous version so I can compare.
evals.expected_output: storyboard outputs cutsheet.html (1 row = 1 cut, first/last frames, start and length in seconds and beats) as v1. Adding feedback/v1.json and re-running gives v2, keeps v1/, shows a "Responses to v1 FB" table at the top, a v1/v2 comparison image for cuts with FB, and a warning for FB without a response. Writing the responses removes the warnings. FB files are part of the approval hash.

feedback.overall: Give it a bit more whitespace overall

cuts.s2: The cards come in too early. Delay them by one beat

feedback.summary: This version fixes s2 and s4 based on the v1 FB.

assertions: storyboard outputs cutsheet.html and first / last images for each cut, with the columns Start (s · beat) / Length / First frame / Last frame / Picture / Motion / Transition to next / Text / Sound / Verify / FB
start and length in both seconds and beats (s4 = 9.5 s = 19 beats in; 2.5 s = 5 beats at 120 BPM)
re-running without FB does not advance the version
adding an FB file and re-running gives v2, keeps v1/, and shows the "Responses to v1 FB" table
FB without a response is warned about, and the warning disappears once a response is written
only cuts with FB get a v1 vs v2 comparison image
image file names do not collide between Japanese cut IDs or with an ASCII ID resembling a replaced name; cuts before the offset show negative beats
the previous version's storyboard.json points to images in the previous version's folder
the date in the cut sheet heading is the local date (not UTC)
bars and cuts in the timeline strip share the same time axis (no drift even with offset > 0)
FB files are part of the approval hash (adding FB after approval stops final)

evals.name: render-contracts
evals.prompt: (internal check) Confirm that the determinism, loop and forbidden-API checks can actually fail, and that the spring and beat-grid math is correct.
evals.expected_output: Detects and fails a render that carries state over from previous frames, a render that uses Math.random, and a loop with an off period. The 4 spring presets converge; default does not overshoot and snappy/playful overshoot slightly.
assertions: check fails for a render that carries state over from previous frames
a render that uses Math.random fails with a reason
a loop with an off period fails at the seam
spring, springTrack and beatGrid math
composition gives the same MIDI for the same input and a different MIDI when style or seed changes
chord name parsing (Cmaj7, slash chords, stops on unreadable names)
